successors.name: Nepal
successors.text: Gorkha and the lands annexed since 1744, with the Kathmandu Valley (the same handover the nepal dossier lists as its predecessor land)

ledger.x: 1559: Dravya Shah founds the Gorkha Kingdom at Gorkha.

ledger.cp: Dolakha and the hill principalities east of the Nepal Valley

ledger.x: 1757: the Gorkhalis open the assault on the Nepal Valley.
1763: the towns on the valley's east and south rim fall.
March 1766: Kirtipur falls after three assaults.
25 September 1768: Prithvi Narayan Shah takes Kathmandu.
25 September 1768: the fight for the valley's first city ends in the Gorkhali entry into Kathmandu; Lalitpur (October 1768) and Bhaktapur (1769) are the nepal dossier's.
1768: the capital passes from Gorkha to Kathmandu ('declared Kathmandu the capital of his unified kingdom'); the Unification table dates 'Kathmandu is declared as the capital' to 1769.
25 September 1768: the Gorkha Kingdom becomes the Kingdom of Nepal.

wars.name: Unification of Nepal
wars.outcome: The Gorkhalis took Nuwakot (1744), Dolakha (1754), Makwanpur (1762), Kirtipur (1766), Kathmandu (25 September 1768) and, in the nepal dossier, Lalitpur (1768) and Bhaktapur (1769); on 25 September 1768 the Kingdom of Nepal was announced.

wars.name: Kinloch expedition (Battle of Sindhuli Gadhi)
wars.outcome: The expedition sent to help the king of Kathmandu 'completely miscarried': 'once the troops reached Sindhuli, the promised help collapsed' (September 1767, Battle of Sindhuli Gadhi).

certainty.note: Hill principalities with no surveyed or treaty boundary on any page; the extent of each annexation is read from district and town names.
